correctness.rationale: For arbitrary integer n>=2 and k>=1, exact barycentric coordinates give a Euclidean separation of n*a/(n-1) for discrepancy a. All accessible grid heights 0,...,sum floor(k lambda_i) are realized exactly. Since the fractional-part sum is an integer at most n-1, every point has distance at most epsilon*min(1,(n-1)/k). For k<n, the centered top-facet point remains epsilon away from the entire average; for k>=n the explicitly constructed barycentric point has floor sum k-n+1 and every higher stratum is horizontally more than epsilon*(n-1)/k away under epsilon<1/(n-1)^2. The same-level witness attains equality. Schneider index n-1 follows from covering the top simplex by vertex-shifted copies at parameter s>=n-1 and overlapping height intervals. Exact-rational checker replayed the algebra and thirteen exhaustively enumerated instances. No finite experiment substitutes for the all-n,all-k proof.

value.rationale: The exact all-order profile supplies the missing quantitative decrease at the first contracting stage of van Hintum’s canonical threshold example. It identifies one compact nonconvex family simultaneously saturating FMMZ’s structurally motivated Schneider-index inequality for every integer averaging order; this directly gives a lower obstruction (n-1)/n for any proposed universal n-fold contraction and shows the coefficient of the index bound cannot be improved in that regime. This solves a natural all-order invariant, not an arbitrary finite parameter recomputation. The universal upper conjecture and largest admissible height are not claimed.
